chapter: Sid Leprotti and the So Different band
title: Sid Leprotti: strokes, character, Canadian Capers, Gerald Wells
summary: Sid Leprotti's New Orleans origins, Australia during the war, many strokes, his secretive manner and his composition Canadian Capers.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Did Sid Leprotti come from New Orleans? That's his hometown.
It was his hometown.
Yeah.
Yeah. But he worked all over, and during the war, he was in Australia. So the whole band enlisted in Australia as a band, so they didn't have to go and fight.
And you worked at Sid Leprotti, huh?
When I got discharged, yeah.
I'd hoped to be able to talk to him, but they say he's had several strokes.
I just was out there Friday and couldn't see him. No, he won't come.
Do you think he'll ever recover now? No.
16 strokes. I don't think he'll make it. He don't know nobody. Really?
He's that bad? Mm-hmm.

Mm-hmm. Do you remember, since he won't be able to talk for himself, can you remember a little bit about his life? Did he ever tell you anything? Where he came, just what part of town? Well, no. Did he ever play with or anything?

No, he was very clandestine. In his younger days, you thought maybe he was white. Mm-hmm. So he carried himself that way, and he always seemed to bend in the money or something. So I never did visit his home and never was that close.
Never did get to hear much about his life?
No.

No. There's one friend of mine once had a little homemade recording of him. I think they took on the job once, so I did get to hear him play Four O'Clock Blues, and I think he played The Pearls, that piece of jelly roll.
Yeah. And he had one number of his own that he used to play all the time, but he sold a copyright. It's called Canadian Capers. Oh, that was his number?
Originally, yeah.
Oh, really?
I never knew that. Mm-hmm.
Mm-hmm. And he sold it so he can't make any claim for it anymore.
Yeah. And he did compose that?
Yeah. He and this fellow, Gerald Wells, he's 72. He lived in Seattle. He quit music altogether, too. He's in the real estate business.
Is he from New Orleans by any chance?
Who, Gerald Wells? Mm-hmm. No, he's a West Indy.

West Indy. Mm-hmm. I wasn't sure Sip, but it probably came from New Orleans, and you're sure of that then? Yeah. He didn't come from his barn down that way. Yeah. Came out here real early and worked at the Barbary Coast.
